title: Flare Screen for a Shooter
description: A screener sets a flare screen to free a shooter moving away from the ball, a common way to create an open three off ball reversal.

content.objective: Set a well-timed flare screen that frees a shooter moving away from the ball.
content.setup: A shooter starts near the elbow; a screener sets up behind the shooter's defender.
instructions: As the ball reverses to the far side, the screener sets a flare screen on the shooter's defender.
The shooter reads the screen and flares out to the corner or wing.
The passer delivers a skip pass to the now-open shooter.
Reset and repeat with the screener and shooter swapping roles.
coachingPoints: Time the screen to arrive just as the defender starts to chase.
The shooter should flare at an angle, not run in a straight line.
The passer must be ready with the skip pass the instant the shooter is open.
commonMistakes: Setting the screen too early, before the defender commits to chasing.
Shooter flaring too slowly and letting the defender recover.
Cutting without actually drawing any real defensive attention.
content.safety: The screener holds a legal, stationary position before contact.
